title: Alvina of the Darkroot Wood
snippet: Alvina thus founded the Forest Hunter covenant, a clan of hunters bound with the aim of protecting the Darkroot Forest where her friend rested and Sif resided from the many adventurers who invaded it in search of the tomb of the legendary knight. Alvina would try to dissuade those who ventured into the region recently, advising them not to seek Artorias' tomb and that his legends were only fabrications and fairy tales.

title: Alvina of the Darkroot Wood
snippet:
Alvina of the Darkroot Wood -  Dark Souls - character - lead 
 lead : **Alvina of the Darkroot Wood** (白猫アルヴィナ), commonly referred to as **Alvina**, is a character in *Dark Souls* who acts the leader of the Forest Hunter covenant. She is voiced by Ève Karpf.

title: Alvina of the Darkroot Wood
snippet:
Alvina of the Darkroot Wood -  Dark Souls - character - plot 
 plot : Alvina inducts the player into the Forest Hunter covenant when answered "Yes" to both of her initial questions. Answering "No" to her first question will cause her to shun the player. Hurting Alvina in any way will not kill her, but it will cause her to disappear. If the player is in the Forest Hunter covenant, attacking her will also count as a betrayal and the NPCs in the forest will become hostile, including Shiva. It is possible to make Alvina neutral again by absolving sins with Oswald of Carim. Alvina will be present and repeat the covenant dialogue.

Killing one intruder as part of the Forest Hunter covenant will result in Alvina giving the player a Divine Blessing. Killing 3 trespassers of The Forest will grant the Ring of Fog.

title: Alvina of the Darkroot Wood
snippet:
Alvina of the Darkroot Wood -  Dark Souls - character - location 
 location : Alvina can be found in Darkroot Garden, in a ruined building past the sealed door that can be opened with the Crest of Artorias. The most direct way to get there is through the sealed door and sticking to the left.

title: Alvina of the Darkroot Wood
snippet:
Alvina of the Darkroot Wood -  Dark Souls - character - description 
 description : Alvina appears to be a large cat, resembling a Great Feline but she is also capable of understanding and talking the human language.

title: Alvina of the Darkroot Wood
snippet:
Alvina of the Darkroot Wood -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : Her name and title, accurately translated from the original Japanese description, should be "Alvina, the White Cat" (白猫アルヴィナ).

title: Alvina of the Darkroot Wood
snippet:
Alvina of the Darkroot Wood -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Alvina is a white Great Feline that had lived for centuries since the early Age of Fire and is capable of human speech. At one point she became a trusted friend of Knight Artorias, one of the Four Knights of Gwyn, as well as his companion Great Grey Wolf Sif.

After Artorias' death, Alvina moved to the ruins of Oolacile, now overgrown and known as the "Darkroot Garden", where the knight had succumbed in his fight against the Abyss of Manus. Sif too had moved here after he survived the battle with Manus and inherited Artorias' divine greatsword and the magical ring that had allowed the knight to cross into the Abyss. The wolf settled in the forest where Artorias' tomb had been erected and, wielding his companion's sword in his jaws, continued to fight to guard Artorias' rest, slaughtering the numerous Undead intent on plundering the tomb of the legendary knight.

title: Alvina of the Darkroot Wood
snippet:
Alvina of the Darkroot Wood -  Dark Souls - character - artorias_of_the_abyss 
 artorias_of_the_abyss : Alvina can be encountered briefly during the events of the *Artorias of the Abyss* DLC, in the Chasm of the Abyss. She cannot be interacted with, in the traditional sense, and has no dialogue.

She is found after falling through an illusory floor, and leads the player to an injured but protected Sif. Here the Chosen Undead may choose to secure the white wolf by clearing the area of humanity phantoms, receiving the Cleansing Greatshield as a gift.

Elizabeth pledges to tell future generations that Artorias defeated Manus and halted the Abyss, appearing to confirm that at least part of Artorias' legend was indeed a fabrication, though he was nevertheless a brave and extremely powerful knight.

title: Bed of Chaos
snippet:
Bed of Chaos -  Dark Souls - boss - lead 
 lead : The **Bed of Chaos** (混沌の苗床) is a boss in *Dark Souls*. A hideous lifeform which the Witch of Izalith has turned into, it is found in what remains of her land, Lost Izalith. It is a "puzzle boss" with unconventional mechanics.

Although the traditional way of reaching the Bed involves slaying both the Demon Firesage and the Centipede Demon, a shortcut can be opened by offering Quelaag's Sister 30 Humanity through the Chaos Servant covenant.

title: Bed of Chaos
snippet:
Another common strategy is to summon one or two phantoms and position both next to each orb, with the host out of reach of the Bed of Chaos' arm sweeps, but in a direct line towards the entrance to the core. After both phantoms break the orbs, the host can then head to the entrance of its mouth and kill the boss.
A simple solo strategy involves "corpse-running" to the fog door and then running to each orb and then to the Bed of Chaos itself. Some players prefer to stay hollowed so that humanity is not wasted, since many deaths may follow after the first orb breaks.
Players with a high number of Humanities or souls may be interested in investing in some Rings of Sacrifice.
The chaos scythe/fire pick(s) attacks will almost always miss unless the player stays in one spot for too long.
Its bug-like core is immune to fire damage.
It is possible to make the Bed of Chaos's arm push the player towards the branch that leads to the core.

title: Bed of Chaos
snippet:
The greatest concerns to the player over the encounter will be dealing with the boss' broad, sweeping attacks and the large, bottomless holes that open in different parts of the arena.
Once both roots have been cut, the player must reach the boss' heart to access and kill the Chaos Bug, however it is important to be aware that directly in front of the boss is a large bottomless hole. The primary way across is a wide branch that runs from the boss toward where the encounter begins, just below the height of the floor.
A relatively safe method of dealing with both attacks and holes is to hug the walls around the outside of the arena, on the ledges behind the holes and out of reach of the boss (though, not the Volcanic Chaos attack, see below). From here, the player may sprint and jump to cross the holes and reach the orbs if their weight is low enough, or attack the branches and roots from range with magic or a bow.

title: Bed of Chaos
snippet:
Bed of Chaos -  Dark Souls - boss - strategy 
 strategy : Unlike most boss encounters, the goal here is not to whittle away the boss's health, but to strike at three vulnerable nodes. Thus, the difficulty in defeating this boss mostly lies in discovering the points to strike while avoiding being knocked in a hole rather than in defeating the boss via conventional methods.
The vulnerable nodes are two roots within glowing spheres, visible to the right and left of the boss at the start of the encounter, and the Chaos Bug within this boss' heart. Striking the roots expands the boss' list of available attacks and 'unlocks' access to the boss' heart.
It is also noteworthy that progress made in damaging one or both of the roots does not reset upon the player's death, allowing repeated attempts at the boss to add incremental progress to the encounter.

title: Bed of Chaos
snippet:
Bed of Chaos -  Dark Souls - boss - trivia 
 trivia : In internal game files, the Bed of Chaos is referred to as "King Izalith" ().

title: Bed of Chaos
snippet:
Its bug-like core is immune to fire damage.
It is possible to make the Bed of Chaos's arm push the player towards the branch that leads to the core.
Magic Shield and Strong Magic Shield can be extremely useful against Bed of Chaos, as they can easily block both the scythe and swiping attack with a medium shield without breaking player's guard. This creates a relatively long opening and player can use the remaining stamina to quickly run towards the heart/orb and deal the fatal blow. Lingering Dragoncrest Ring is recommended to counter the short duration of both spells.
One last potential strategy involves the use of shields with high stability. By two-handing a shield such as Havel's Greatshield, and with sufficient Stamina, a player can become almost completely immune to both the damage and knockback effects of the Bed of Chaos's sweeping attacks.

title: Bed of Chaos
snippet:
Bed of Chaos -  Dark Souls - boss - attacks 
 attacks : {'name': 'Flame Aura', 'description': 'Used if the player lingers at the mouth of the Tree Beast without going inside. The Fire Aspect crosses its arms and then swings them open after a distinctive shriek, engulfing the entire area in fire. Hits multiple times.'}

title: Blade of the Darkmoon
snippet:
Blade of the Darkmoon -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Blade of the Darkmoon** (暗月の剣) is a PvP-oriented covenant in *Dark Souls*. Darkmoon Blades hunt those who have sinned.

title: Blade of the Darkmoon
snippet:
Blade of the Darkmoon -  Dark Souls - mechanic - betrayal 
 betrayal : Entering Gwyn's Tomb to confront Gwyndolin counts as a betrayal and results in expulsion from the covenant. Destroying the illusion of Gwynevere while being part of the Blades of the Darkmoon will NOT cause Gwyndolin to expel the player from the covenant, but it will prevent the player from offering any more souvenirs of reprisal to Gwyndolin.

title: Blade of the Darkmoon
snippet:
Blade of the Darkmoon -  Dark Souls - mechanic - overview 
 overview : Blade of the Darkmoon is considered one of the more difficult covenants to master. Every person the player invades as a spirit of vengeance has likely had experience in PvP (since Indictments during an invasion are one of the few repeatable ways of gaining sin), and so will usually put up a tougher fight than people invaded by Darkwraiths. To make matters worse, people in Dark Anor Londo are likely to be duel-mongerers who kill Blades of the Darkmoon for sport or for souls. They very often have friendly summons with them.

However, the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant is very worthwhile. The Darkmoon Talisman has the best miracle adjust in the game, so any player who relies on miracles would benefit from joining this covenant; in turn, Darkmoon Blade is an excellent weapon buff. With patience and perseverance, players may yet reap the benefits of the Blade of the Darkmoon.

title: Blade of the Darkmoon
snippet:
Blade of the Darkmoon -  Dark Souls - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : First, acquire the Darkmoon Seance Ring in The Catacombs. Go to the bottom level of the rotating elevator in Anor Londo to find the Darkmoon Tomb bonfire. Past the bonfire, Gwyn's statue will disappear to reveal a fog gate if the player is wearing the Darkmoon Seance Ring. If the player has killed Gwynevere, the statue will just disappear when approached. Go toward the fog gate and Dark Sun Gwyndolin will ask the player to swear fealty to the Blades of the Darkmoon. Kneel at the fog door to join the covenant.

title: Blade of the Darkmoon
snippet:
Blade of the Darkmoon -  Dark Souls - mechanic - activities 
 activities : Blades of the Darkmoon hunt players that have attacked the illusion of Gwynevere or have committed any amount of sins by either getting kicked out of a covenant or being indicted by other players. Players risk nothing invading other people's worlds (cannot be indicted and all souls and humanity are kept upon death) and gain a Souvenir of Reprisal for each guilty player they defeat.

Outside of Gwyndolin, the only character part of the covenant is the Anor Londo Fire Keeper, although she does not provide a fellow Darkmoon Blade with anything besides unique dialogue. Attacking Gwynevere or passing through Gwyndolin's fog gate will result in her turning hostile, but killing the Fire Keeper will not count as betraying the covenant.

title: Blade of the Darkmoon
snippet:
Blade of the Darkmoon -  Dark Souls - mechanic - known_members 
 known_members : Darkmoon Knightess
Greatsword-wielding Darkmoon Soldier
Straight Sword-wielding Darkmoon Soldier

title: Blade of the Darkmoon
snippet:
Blade of the Darkmoon -  Dark Souls - mechanic - benefits 
 benefits : Upon joining, players receive:
Blue Eye Orb
Darkmoon Blade Covenant Ring

Souvenirs of Reprisal are offered to Dark Sun Gwyndolin to gain ranks in the Blade of the Darkmoon Covenant.

Players may only use the Darkmoon Blade miracle when they are in the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant; the buff is initially 1.8x of the magic adjust of the talisman, but will gain 0.1 with every level gained in the covenant (1.9x at +1, 2.0x at +2, and 2.1x at +3).

Being part of the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant does not prevent invasions from other members.

title: Blade of the Darkmoon
snippet:
Blade of the Darkmoon -  Dark Souls - mechanic - requirements 
 requirements : The player must not have killed Dark Sun Gwyndolin. If the player has killed Gwynevere, they must request absolution from Oswald before joining.

title: Blue Eye Orb
snippet:
Blue Eye Orb -  Dark Souls - item - availability 
 availability : Granted after joining the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant.

title: Blue Eye Orb
snippet:
Blue Eye Orb -  Dark Souls - item - description 
 description : Online play item. Invade world of player in Book of the Guilty. Subdue player to acquire Souvenir of Reprisal. (Only Covenanter can use the item)

These mystical orbs are granted to Blades of the Darkmoon, knights who serve the Dark Sun Gwyndolin, so that they may serve the Gods in meting out vengeance.

title: Blue Eye Orb
snippet:
Blue Eye Orb -  Dark Souls - item - lead 
 lead : The **Blue Eye Orb** is an online play item in *Dark Souls*.

title: Blue Eye Orb
snippet:
Blue Eye Orb -  Dark Souls - item - general_information 
 general_information : Using the Blue Eye Orb allows the player to attempt to invade the world of players that have been indicted. The player must be in the Blades of the Darkmoon covenant to use the Blue Eye Orb; unlike the Red Eye Orb, reversed hollowing is not required and a bloodstain is not left behind if the Blade of the Darkmoon is defeated. Upon defeat of the guilty player, the Blade of the Darkmoon will receive a Souvenir of Reprisal and the host's sin is reduced by 1.

title: Blue Sentinels
snippet:
Blue Sentinels -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : Talk to Blue Sentinel Targray, located in the Cathedral of Blue directly after the Old Dragonslayer boss fight. Reaching him before obtaining at least one Token of Fidelty will have him disregard the player, so be sure to find one if you wish to join the covenant. Upon meeting the requirements and accepting Targray's offer, players will be awarded the Guardian's Seal.

title: Blue Sentinels
snippet:
Blue Sentinels -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - notes 
 notes : Talking to Blue Sentinel Targray after achieving rank 3 in the covenant will cause him to give the player his armor set.
As Rank increases, the blue aura that surrounds the player when invading will become more prominent.
Killing Targray will automatically kick you out of the covenant, but temporarily resurrecting him through his gravestone will let you rejoin the covenant.
While ordinary invaders receive souls by killing the host, the only way for Arbiter Spirits to gain souls is by killing phantoms and dark spirits summoned by or invading the host.
Winning the sparring arena counts towards ranking.

title: Blue Sentinels
snippet: They shared lineage with the Way of Blue, which was not an organized religion but "a humble prayer" that spread organically amongst the needy, eventually growing to the point where the towering Cathedral of Blue was built in the heart of Heide, used by the Blue Sentinels as headquarters. The Sentinels were tasked with defending the apostles of Blue from evil spirits as well as traversing space and time via their eye orbs to punish the guilty, similar to their progenitor. Victorious knights were rewarded with miracles of the ancient gods of Anor Londo like Wrath of the Gods and Bountiful Sunlight that had been lost or jealously guarded elsewhere in Drangleic.

title: Blue Sentinels
snippet: Despite Heide's fall, the Blue Sentinels continued to exert considerable influence in countries near Drangleic. In Volgen, a city ruled by the clerics of the Way of Blue, a group calling themselves Blue Sentinels wields significant power, and hold sway over who can engage in trading within the city. Albeit they are not confirmed to be authentic Blue Sentinels, the rule of Volgen by the Way of Blue suggests that the Sentinels are indeed present in the city, as a bottleneck on mercantile competition.

title: Blue Sentinels
snippet:
Blue Sentinels -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The is a PvP-oriented covenant in *Dark Souls II*, devoted to protecting members of the Way of Blue and invading worlds of those who have sinned. It operates much like the Blade of the Darkmoon covenant from *Dark Souls*.

title: Blue Sentinels
snippet:
Blue Sentinels -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lore 
 lore : The Blue Sentinels are direct descendants of the original Blade of the Darkmoon covenant that served Dark Sun Gwyndolin in Anor Londo. The Sentinels were amongst those who left Lordran and reached Drangleic, founding the civilization of Heide as its Knights. These knights still possess the Cracked Blue Eye Orbs, the worn remains of the Blue Eye Orbs granted to the Blades of the Darkmoon who served Gwyndolin to mete out the vengeance of the gods at the times of Anor Londo.

title: Blue Sentinels
snippet:
Blue Sentinels -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - benefits 
 benefits : After joining the covenant, Targray can teach the player the Duel Bow gesture, he also sells a few common weapons like the Halberd, healing items like the Monastery Charm, and the Holy Water Urns.
He also sells the miracles Heavenly Thunder and Emit Force.
The player receives the Guardian's Seal, which will allow them to be summoned as an Arbiter Spirit by Way of Blue covenant members in order to help them defeat the invader that triggered the summon. A Token of Fidelity will be rewarded after the invader has been killed.
Members of the covenant also have the ability to use Cracked Blue Eye Orbs to invade the worlds of the guilty.
With a Token of Fidelity, players can interact with the statues near the Blue Cathedral bonfire to enter a PvP arena to fight other members of the Blue Sentinels.

title: Blue Sentinels
snippet: The civilization of Heide was at some point lost to rising sea levels. While large sections were reduced to half-submerged rubble, the upper sections and the Tower of Flame were left intact, which continued to host the Blue Sentinels. With Targray at the helm, the Sentinels maintained their watch over the apostles of Blue; they even took on new recruits, for whom the Heide Knights, the Old Knights and an Old Dragonslayer served as initiation into the covenant. Those who proved their mettle gained access to the covenant leader, and could use the Cracked Blue Eye Orbs they pillaged from the knights to enact divine vengeance against sinners.

title: Blue Sentinels
snippet:
Blue Sentinels -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - mechanics 
 mechanics : A Blue Sentinel invading a guilty player with the Cracked Blue Eye Orb seems to favor invading players generally below the player's Soul Memory.
**This contrasts the Brotherhood of Blood members, who generally invade players above their own Soul Memory using the Cracked Red Eye Orb.
The Blue Sentinel can also use the Guardian's Seal to assist players against invaders, as long as the invader isn't also an Arbiter Spirit.

title: Blue Sentinels
snippet:
Blue Sentinels -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - requirements 
 requirements : Players must have one Token of Fidelity in their possession, which can be obtained either by defeating a boss in another player's world as a phantom, or by finding one hidden away in Huntsman's Copse for those who are playing offline. Alternatively, they can be obtained in NG+ or when Heide's Tower of Flame is at Bonfire intensity 2 by burning a Bonfire Ascetic, as Dark Spirits resembling Blue Sentinels will spawn and drop a token each when slain.

title: Brotherhood of Blood
snippet:
Brotherhood of Blood -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - requirements 
 requirements : Players must have one Token of Spite in their possession, which can be obtained either by defeating a the host of another world or their assisting Arbiter Spirit as a Dark Spirit, or by finding one hidden on the way to the Gutter for those who are playing offline. Alternatively, they can be obtained in NG+ or when Heide's Tower of Flame is at Bonfire intensity 2 by burning a Bonfire Ascetic, as a Dark Spirit resembling an Executioner will spawn and drop a token when slain.

title: Brotherhood of Blood
snippet:
Brotherhood of Blood -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The is a PvP-oriented covenant in *Dark Souls II*, encouraging invasions and rewarding players who manage to kill the host of the invaded world. It operates much like the Darkwraith covenant from *Dark Souls*.

title: Brotherhood of Blood
snippet:
Brotherhood of Blood -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lore 
 lore : The Brotherhood of Blood is a mysterious cult whose members are devoted to Nahr Alma, the god of blood. The members of this bloodthirsty covenant are tasked with collecting blood in order to offer it as a sacrifice to Nahr Alma. According to Titchy Gren, the members of the Brotherhood of Blood have a feud with the Blue Sentinels, mainly due to the opposite objectives of both covenants.

title: Brotherhood of Blood
snippet:
Brotherhood of Blood -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : Talk to Titchy Gren, located in the Undead Purgatory directly after the Executioner's Chariot boss fight. Reaching him before obtaining at least one Token of Spite will have him disregard the player, so be sure to find one if you wish to join the covenant. Upon meeting the requirements and confirming your desire of bathing in blood to Titchy Gren multiple times, players will be awarded the Crest of Blood.

title: Brotherhood of Blood
snippet:
Brotherhood of Blood -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - notes 
 notes : Invasions and duels in the Undead Purgatory are separated from one another, meaning that the player's rank will not level up from both invasions and duels. For instance, if a player with base rank has 25 dueling wins and 25 invasion kills, their rank will still remain at zero. Invasions with cracked red eye orbs do NOT count towards your total.
Losses in dueling or invasions will subtract one kill from the player's overall kill count for the respective area.
**If a player has 50 dueling wins and an equal amount of losses, their kill count will be zero.
**If a player has 50 dueling wins followed by 100 dueling losses, their kill count will be zero, not -50. It is not possible to achieve a negative overall kill count in the dueling arena.
Duels from a Red Sign Soapstone do not count towards your rank.
Killing Gren will automatically kick you out of the covenant.

title: Brotherhood of Blood
snippet:
Brotherhood of Blood -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - benefits 
 benefits : Upon joining the covenant, Titchy Gren will give the player the Crest of Blood, be available as a merchant, and will sell various wares to the player including spells, ammunition, armor, and in NG+, Cracked Red Eye Orbs.
When dueling another player via the statues at the Undead Purgatory, the victor receives a Cracked Red Eye Orb.
If the members of this covenant have won a certain number of arena duels and rank up, they will show a distinctive glowing red aura surrounding them while in red phantom form.

Upon reaching certain arena victory milestones, the player will receive the following rewards:

title: Brotherhood of Blood
snippet:
Duels from a Red Sign Soapstone do not count towards your rank.
Killing Gren will automatically kick you out of the covenant.
The Brotherhood of Blood was one of the three available covenants in the network test.
If one is not interested in dueling, the covenant rewards can be gotten in other ways:
**The Crest of Blood is obtained simply by joining the covenant.
**Gren will drop the Nahr Alma Hood upon death, and the Robes and Scythe will then be sold by Merchant Hag Melentia.
**Chancellor Wellager will sell the Curved Twinblade, Crescent Sickle, and Great Chaos Fireball in NG++.

title: Cat Covenant Ring
snippet:
Removing the ring when in the target's world will not cause the player to return to their homeworld.

Successfully killing a player as a Forest Hunter invader will raise the Forest Hunter's rank and reward them with an item.

The Cat Covenant Ring stays with the player if they leave or betray the covenant, but will not function while not formally affiliated.

If the ring is lost by any means, it will reappear in the chest behind Kingseeker Frampt after reloading an area.

title: Cat Covenant Ring
snippet:
Cat Covenant Ring -  Dark Souls - ring - general_information 
 general_information : The Cat Covenant Ring will add Forest Hunter players who wear it to an invasion queue. Those players will be sent to invade the worlds of non-Forest Hunter players who enter Darkroot Forest to kill them.

Unlike normal invasions, the Forest Hunter invasions can be performed even by hollow players and from anywhere in the game world (except for those areas without an associated boss, such as Firelink Shrine or Gwynevere's chamber in Anor Londo). There is no level restriction, meaning someone of low level such as 40 can invade anyone, so they could be paired with a level 200. The invaders lose nothing should they fail, including their non-hollowed state. Invaders who die will be returned to the last bonfire they visited with all items, souls, and humanity intact.

Removing the ring when in the target's world will not cause the player to return to their homeworld.

title: Cat Covenant Ring
snippet:
Cat Covenant Ring -  Dark Souls - ring - lead 
 lead : The **Cat Covenant Ring** is a ring in *Dark Souls*.

title: Cat Covenant Ring
snippet:
Cat Covenant Ring -  Dark Souls - ring - availability 
 availability : The Cat Covenant Ring is obtained by joining the Forest Hunter covenant in Darkroot Forest.

title: Cat Covenant Ring
snippet:
Cat Covenant Ring -  Dark Souls - ring - description 
 description : Ring granted to those bound by the Forest Hunter covenant.
Answer Alvina's summoning.

The white cat Alvina speaks a human tongue and has lived since the early Age of Fire. Alvina was a trusted friend of Knight Artorias and the Great Wolf Sif.

title: Cat Covenant Ring
snippet:
Cat Covenant Ring -  Dark Souls - ring - notes 
 notes : It is possible to farm souls from this ring as it can never be permanently lost. Feeding it to Kingseeker Frampt will result in 1,000 souls, and the ring can then be retrieved from the chest behind him after reloading the area.

title: Chaos Servant
snippet: Humanities are offered to Quelaag's Sister to gain ranks in the Chaos Servant Covenant.

title: Chaos Servant
snippet:
Chaos Servant -  Dark Souls - mechanic - notes 
 notes : Eingyi will sell a Servant Roster to the player which can keep track of the amount of humanity other Chaos Servants have donated.
If the player becomes infected with eggs by an Egg Burdened, Eingyi will also sell the player the Poison Mist and Toxic Mist pyromancies.
If the player wears the Old Witch's Ring, they become able to understand Quelaag's Sister.
It is important to note that to access the Lost Izalith shortcut, players must be in that covenant when activating it.

title: Chaos Servant
snippet:

 notable_members : Chaos Witch Quelaag
The Fair Lady
Eingyi
**Kirk, Knight of Thorns*

title: Chaos Servant
snippet:
Chaos Servant -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Chaos Servant** (混沌の従者) is a covenant in *Dark Souls*. Chaos Servants dedicate themselves to the Fair Lady and provide her with humanity.

title: Chaos Servant
snippet:
Chaos Servant -  Dark Souls - mechanic - requirements 
 requirements : The player must not have killed Quelaag's Sister.

title: Chaos Servant
snippet:
Chaos Servant -  Dark Souls - mechanic - benefits 
 benefits : Attain the Great Chaos Fireball pyromancy upon joining. After reaching rank +2, players also attain the Chaos Storm (an upgraded version of Firestorm)
Access to the shortcut to Lost Izalith (the shortcut can be found to the right, before the Demon Firesage boss in the Demon Ruins). The shortcut is one of two ways to save Solaire of Astora.
To open the shortcut door, 30 Humanity must be given **only one time per character**. In subsequent playthroughs on the same character the shortcut door will open as long as the player has currently joined the Chaos Servant Covenant, regardless of rank. The Fair Lady must be alive for the door to open.
Players may also reach rank +2 in the covenant and leave, then rejoin to open the shortcut door. Holding the Chaos Storm pyromancy while being in the covenant with the Fair Lady alive appears to be the "key" to this door regardless of current rank.

title: Chaos Servant
snippet:
Chaos Servant -  Dark Souls - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : After defeating Chaos Witch Quelaag, reach the circular room beneath the Bell of Awakening where there are cobwebs lining eggs on the sides. The wall to the right is illusory. Inside, there will be an egg-infected man named Eingyi. The player must answer "Yes" to his question in order for him to move. If the player has answered "No", quitting and reloading will prompt Eingyi to pose his question again. The player may also kill him and join without repercussion. However, this will cost the player his services. Talking to Quelaag's Sister will give the option to join the covenant.

title: Cleric
snippet:
At an initial level of 2, Clerics have the second-lowest starting level (the lowest being Pyromancers) of any class. They start the game as a member of the Way of White covenant.

Joining the Warriors of Sunlight can allow Clerics to become powerful magical attackers early on in the game, giving them the miracle Lightning Spear. Astora's Straight Sword and Dragon Crest Shield are also very useful early game pick-ups for the Cleric, provided they choose the Master Key as their gift and enter Valley of Drakes via New Londo Ruins. The former scales with Faith, allowing the Cleric to focus exclusively on it, while the latter is a far better shield than that which the Cleric starts with.

title: Cleric
snippet:
Cleric -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Cleric** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls*.

Clerics can use miracles to heal, due to their high starting Faith stat and equipped Talisman. They also start with a strong melee weapon in the form of the Mace, but little in the way of defense. Clerics are well suited to heavier weapon types, such as Hammers, as taking on enemies directly with slower weapons is offset by their ability to heal more often than other classes.

At an initial level of 2, Clerics have the second-lowest starting level (the lowest being Pyromancers) of any class. They start the game as a member of the Way of White covenant.

title: Covenant
snippet:
Covenant -  Dark Souls - mechanic - general_information 
 general_information : There are nine covenants in all. Some covenants have four ranks, from 0 to +3. Ranking up in a covenant can bring additional rewards.

title: Covenant
snippet:
Covenant -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : A **covenant** is a faction that a player may join in *Dark Souls*. Being part of a covenant grants various benefits, though it also imposes certain rules on the player. Breaking said rules can lead to negative effects. Covenants may also have an effect on the player's online interactions.

title: Covenant
snippet:
Covenant -  Dark Souls - mechanic - changing_covenants 
 changing_covenants : Players may only join one covenant at a time. Should players wish to join a different covenant, it is necessary to break their contract with their previous covenant first, through betrayal, through Oswald, the pardoner, or by changing covenants at a bonfire (Remastered only). It is recommended to change covenants through Oswald, covenant leaders, or at a bonfire, as killing covenant leaders will often lead to much harsher penalties than simply changing covenants

Upon leaving a covenant, even with through Oswald, half of the progress the player has made in ranking up in the covenant is lost, should they wish to rejoin later. For example, having offered 30 humanity to a covenant will be reduced to 15 if one should rejoin and want to attain the previously held rank.

title: Covenant
snippet: It is possible to be kicked out of four of the covenants: Blade of the Darkmoon, Princess's Guard, Chaos Servant, and Forest Hunter. When kicked out of a covenant, any offerings made to that covenant will be reduced to 0 and requesting absolution will be required to rejoin the covenant, provided that the covenant leader is still alive.

title: Dark Chasm of Old
snippet: After completing three challenges, the end of the last area cleared will lead the player to face a boss: the Darklurker. Killing him will grant the player victory and the final rank in the covenant.

title: Dark Chasm of Old
snippet:
Dark Chasm of Old -  Dark Souls II - location - trivia 
 trivia : Some of the blue phantoms resemble old characters from the first *Dark Souls*: Havel the Rock, Undead Prince Ricard, and Xanthous King Jeremiah.

title: Dark Chasm of Old
snippet:
Dark Chasm of Old -  Dark Souls II - location - shaded_woods 
 shaded_woods : There are four enemies in this chasm. Follow the path until it opens up, and then follow the left wall downward in the next room where there will be three enemies: a shade and two black phantoms. Try luring them one at a time with magic or arrows. The shade has the least health, and a pit can be found directly ahead of the entrance, try positioning an enemy's back towards the pit and attack them so they stagger backwards and fall down the pit to their deaths. When the room is clear, light the sconce. At the end of the room (watch out for holes) is a switch that will bring up a lift; go down it to fight one last black phantom in a very open area with completely solid ground. Once the phantom has been defeated, the exit pit on the right will open.

title: Dark Chasm of Old
snippet:
Once he's taken care of, a shade can be found to the left, Undead Prince Ricard in a tunnel straight ahead (which also joins to the left), and a female phantom who inflicts Bleed to the right. The latter is fought in an area with a pit in the center, and it is fairly easy to position her back towards it and attack her until she falls down.

The sconce is on the left path, and the exit pit is on the right, just past the female phantom.

title: Dark Chasm of Old
snippet:
Dark Chasm of Old -  Dark Souls II - location - lead 
 lead : The **Dark Chasm of Old** (古き闇の穴, *Furuki yami no ana*) is a location in *Dark Souls II*. It is only accessible through the Pilgrims of Dark covenant.

title: Dark Chasm of Old
snippet:
Dark Chasm of Old -  Dark Souls II - location - notes 
 notes : Quitting and rejoining the covenant will not give the player a free attempt; after the very first try, they will always need to give Darkdiver Grandahl a Human Effigy.
Even if one fails to defeat the Darklurker, they will still have cleared the last challenge they were doing.
**Players will have to clear out an area again on subsequent attempts to face the Darklurker.
Once the Darklurker has been defeated, the player will get the final rank and unlimited access to the Dark Chasm of Old on any location.

title: Dark Chasm of Old
snippet:
Dark Chasm of Old -  Dark Souls II - location - black_gulch 
 black_gulch : There are six enemies in this chasm. At the end of the short path, three enemies will block the player's way, and it is important not to draw all of their aggro at once. Use arrows or slowly edge along the right until the Ironclad phantom with two weapons comes after the player; sometimes the shade will come after the player too. Ideally, the pyromancer at the bottom will not notice the player. Kill the shade first if it notices the player as it has the least health, otherwise concentrate on the Ironclad phantom. When they have both been defeated, clear out the pyromancer as well.

title: Dark Chasm of Old
snippet:
The beacons that must be lit are a large black bowl with a little metal part one can interact with; it must be lit by using a torch that itself must be lit with a Flame Butterfly; one may see when they are approaching the bowl by the surrounding black columns on the walls. The sconce cannot be lit using Pyromancy, thus it may be a good idea to stock up on Flame Butterflies if one is low – Weaponsmith Ornifex sells them.

When one first enters the covenant, the portal will be open, but subsequent attempts at the Dark Chasm of Old requires the player give Grandahl a Human Effigy to reopen the portal. Considering the many deadly falls in the chasm and the enemies that boast high HP, this can be a potentially costly procedure if one dies a lot. If the player dies inside the Dark Chasm, they will return to the last bonfire rested at.

title: Dark Chasm of Old

title: Dark Chasm of Old
snippet:
Dark Chasm of Old -  Dark Souls II - location - achievements_trophies 
 achievements_trophies : Although there is no dedicated Achievement/Trophy for completing the Dark Chasm of Old or defeating the Darklurker, there are two hexes that can only be unlocked through completion of these areas.

Climax is unlocked after completing all three areas of the Dark Chasm of Old and defeating the Darklurker. Return and speak to Darkdiver Grandahl to advance to the third and final rank of the Pilgrims of Dark covenant, whereupon Grandahl will reward the player with this hex.

Lifedrain Patch requires that the player trade the Darklurker Soul and 5,000 Souls to Straid of Olaphis at The Lost Bastille (players will need a Fragrant Branch of Yore to free him if they have not done so first).

title: Dark Chasm of Old
snippet: drangleic_castle : When the player arrives, they should be careful, as they can fall down and die instantly if they don't watch where they step; the path twists in an 'S' shape, so stick to the path and head through the door way. Lighting a torch using a Flame Butterfly can help here, or just simply move the camera overhead and aim it directly downwards. The path will open up in to a wider area with split ways. On the left will be the first black spirit who resembles Havel the Rock: a heavily armored knight equipped with a Dragon Tooth. Havel is the most deadly opponent in this area; his attacks drain a lot of stamina and can forcibly send the player backwards a great deal, even off the edge. Powerful magic works well against him, and if one is skilled or daring, they can fight him near the edge and attack him until he falls off it, instantly killing him. Much like in the first game, he can also be backstabbed, which helps immensely.

title: Dark Chasm of Old
snippet: Further on, when the path forks left and right, go left to light the sconce. Be careful when walking towards the sconce as the pathway is on the right and a large pit lies on the left. Return to where the path forked and go to the right this time, leading to the exit, which is again guarded by the same three enemies. Again, try to lure the Ironclad phantom out first, then deal with the shade too if it comes after the player, and then the pyromancer. After all enemies are defeated, the fog covering the exit pit dissipates and one can leave.

title: Dark Chasm of Old
snippet:
Dark Chasm of Old -  Dark Souls II - location - overview 
 overview : This location is accessible via a magic portal located at any of the three places one can find Darkdiver Grandahl in; each location the player can access the Dark Chasm of Old from offers a different area. Each area challenges the player with lighting a sconce with a torch, killing all of the black phantoms so the fog wall covering the exit disappears, and then finally jumping through a dark, foggy pit which will teleport the player either back to Grandahl or, if all three areas have been successfully cleared out and their beacons lit, to the Darklurker.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet: Gwyndolin thus continued to remain hidden in his father's empty mausoleum, administering Anor Londo from the shadows and continuing to carry out his father's will to uphold the Age of Fire, punishing sinners and leading the Undead without revealing himself. At some point, he was visited by an Undead woman. The woman entered his service as a Blade of the Darkmoon and became the sole Fire Keeper in Anor Londo, although whether she was already a Keeper or became one upon entering his service is unclear. He gifted this "Darkmoon Knightess" with a golden armor set to hide her own "hideous form", as well as his Darkmoon special talisman and Darkmoon Blade miracle. The Knightess assisted in Gwyndolin's attempt of fulfilling his father's prophecy, offering Undead who reached Anor Londo her kindled bonfire, and some guidance, first towards the illusion of Gwynevere, or, if they have already obtained the Lordvessel from the illusion, with information on Seath the Scaleless, the nearest of the

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet:
Dark Sun Gwyndolin -  Dark Souls III - boss - notes 
 notes : Gwyndolin's corridor is not infinite and has a certain length. If he is forced to the end of the corridor, he won't be able to teleport anymore and will be at the player's mercy. He will attack relentlessly, trying to defend himself, but as his attacks are mostly designed for long range battle, just circling him will make most of them miss.
Defeating Gwyndolin grants Domhnall the ability to sell the Moonlight Set; most notably his helmet, which increases the power of all magic.
The Darkmoon Knightess will become hostile if Gwyndolin has been challenged, regardless of whether he was defeated or not.
**Likewise, if Gwynevere was slain, the Darkmoon Knightess will become hostile as well, as such an act will be considered an offense against Gwyndolin.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet:
Dark Sun Gwyndolin -  Dark Souls III - boss - dark_souls 
 dark_souls : Gwyndolin is the lastborn child of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight and one of the deities who resided in Anor Londo during the Age of Fire, although his legitimacy as such only came from being a child of his father. He was worshipped as the "God of the Darkmoon" and held the title of "God of the Dark Sun".

Despite being the son of Gwyn, Gwyndolin was born with a strong moon power, and "weak and repulsive" in appearance, particularly due to the snakes coiled around his lower half. Because of his darkmoon powers and his strong affinity for moon magic, as well as his lineage, Gwyndolin was raised as a female. While still young, Gwyn made him wear women's clothing and gave him a magic ring which would allow Gwyndolin to move and act in a feminine way, leading him to behave "like a dark and fleeting goddess".

title: Sunlight Spear (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Sunlight Spear (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - spell - effect 
 effect : The strongest variant of the Lightning Spear family of Miracles. Conjures a deep-colored spear made of Lightning, then hurls it at the target. The projectile inflicts 2.6 times the Spell Buff of the catalyst as Lightning damage.

When cast at extremely close range, the spear will inflict an additional 1.9 times the Spell Buff of the catalyst as Lightning damage. A successful point-blank cast will also result in vibration feedback through the player's controller, providing confirmation of inflicting additional damage.

While extremely damaging, Sunlight Spear is also very costly in terms of FP.

title: Sunlight Spear
snippet:
Sunlight Spear -  Dark Souls - spell - general_information 
 general_information : Sunlight Spear requires the user to be a Warrior of Sunlight to cast. At first glance, it appears identical to Great Lightning Spear save for its coloration and number of casts. Like the other Lightning Spear variants, it also causes a large cascade of electrical energy if thrown into water, potentially hitting multiple foes.

It has a lightning attack power equal to 3.7 times the talisman's magic adjust, and deals high Poise damage; making it more likely that an opponent will be knocked down if it hits.

Although Sunlight Spear deals more damage than Great Lightning Spear, it comes with half the casts while occupying two slots. In addition, Sunlight Spear requires 50 Faith, reducing its accessibility compared to other Lightning Spear varieties.

title: Miracle (Dark Souls II)
snippet: Not many enemies in the core game are resistant to Lightning damage and enemies that are Waterlogged take more damage from lightning. As such, miracles such as Great Lightning Spearand Sunlight Blade are always a reliable form of elemental damage to have on hand. Enemies from the DLCs boast higher elemental defenses and as such can be difficult to surmount with offensive miracles alone.

title: Lightning Spear
snippet:
Lightning Spear -  Dark Souls - spell - overview 
 overview : Lightning Spear is a good long-range way of greeting enemies. It deals respectable damage and can be used often thanks to its generous amount of uses. Lightning Spear deals lightning damage, which helps diversify the types of damage a player can deal.

In PvP, Lightning Spear is risky to use due to its long casting time and its lack of AoE damage without hitting a body of water which aren't very abundant. However, it deals good damage if it connects due to the lower lightning resistance most players possess. In any situation, Great Lightning Spear is superior due to its greater damage and no drawbacks.

title: Lightning Spear
snippet:
Lightning Spear -  Dark Souls - spell - general_information 
 general_information : It has a lightning attack power equal to 2.7 times the talisman's magic adjust.

Lightning Spear is one of the few offensive miracles and also one of the only spells that inflict lightning damage. It features a long casting time, pin-point accuracy, and a very long effective range (a good deal longer than lock-on range, although manual aiming can be tricky).

As with most other miracles, Lightning Spear scales with Faith and the type of Talisman it is cast by. Throwing Lightning Spear and its variants into water will cause lightning damage to radiate from the point of impact.

title: Dragonslayer Spear
snippet: An easy way to obtain the Dragonslayer Spear is to downgrade the Lightning Spear dropped by the Mimic in Sen's Fortress to a +10 Spear, and then upgrading it to the Dragonslayer Spear. However, a +5 Dragonslayer Spear will not significantly outperform a +5 Lightning Spear at lower Faith levels (~16 or below) until the user well exceeds the required levels in Strength or Dexterity. A fully-upgraded Demon's Spear also has a higher overall damage rating at low Faith levels, and deals more Lightning damage at Faith levels of 42 and below. This weapon cannot be Enchanted and almost any buffable weapon of any class will out-perform this Spear in terms of damage potential.

title: Spear of the Church
snippet: There is no single strategy against a Spear of the Church, as the builds and approaches differ from player to player. One must be prepared for the gimmicks unique to the fight though, as the summoned enemy will always have increased defenses, as well as projectiles of light that will occasionally appear above them automatically and aim for the player while turning into the shape of a spear tip, working similarly to the Homing Soulmass sorcery. The more summons the player has, the more frequently these bullets of light will appear. Other tools at their disposal are the Ritual Spear Fragment and its upgrade, the Divine Spear Fragment, an item granted only to those who achive the top rank in their covenant. Both items spawn a row of spears of light that thrust upwards from the ground and leave a sort of electrified trail. As a way to help the player, Spears of the Church cannot use their Estus Flasks to heal, but can still cast healing miracles, or get healed by the Church Guardians.

 overview : Of the three light sources available to the player (the Skull Lantern, the Sunlight Maggot, and the Cast Light sorcery), the Skull Lantern can easily be considered the worst option due to the effect being active only when the player raises it, and especially because it forces the player to sacrifice his/her shield. title: Black Witch's Staff
snippet:
Melee attacking with the staff, while having moderately low attack speed and short reach, deals impressive damage as it has damage values and scaling with all four elemental damage types.

It does suffer from poor stat scaling on Lightning damage, making it inferior to most sacred chimes in terms of using Lightning Spear or similar abilities. It also cannot be infused with Lightning, unlike chimes. This makes it excel with miracles that do not scale with lightning damage, such as Heal or Great Magic Barrier.

title: Abbess Feeva
snippet:
Abbess Feeva -  Dark Souls II - character - strategy 
 strategy : She only uses miracles such as Great Lightning Spear and Blinding Bolt in combat, can cast Sacred Oath and will heal the party with Soothing Sunlight if a party member's HP is reduced to a dangerously low amount. Considering Sinh has fairly high elemental defenses, she doesn't have the ability to do sufficient damage to the dragon, so her strong points are supporting the party and tanking hits.

title: The Nameless King
snippet: The Falconers, a group of mercenaries hired to protect the elites of Volgen, were still part of the covenant of those that worshipped the God of the Sun and possessed their Sunlight Medals. Moreover, in Lindelt, a "sacred land" known for its clerics and miracles, the Nameless King's miracles of Lightning Spear and Great Lightning Spear were preserved and passed down within its religion, although the names of the clan of gods and the sun god had been lost. Furthermore, some other miracles of the god such as the Sunlight Blade and the Sacred Oath appear to have been part of the lost culture of Olaphis, indicating a continuing tradition of the cult of the Nameless King, even if fragmentary, throughout the history of Drangleic.

title: The Imperfect
snippet:
They seem to have no significant defenses, allowing almost any weapon types or elements to deal consistent damage. Even though most of their attacks can be blocked, they can do significant stamina damage. If in melee range, the player must be ready to roll away if the Imperfect gets ready to stomp or jump, as both attacks will deal significant damage, and knock the player down.

Area of effect miracles like Heavenly Thunder and Splintering Lightning Spear are very effective against them. Note that during their stomp attack and biting grab attack their defense is greatly increased so it is advised to save such spell uses for when they are vulnerable.

title: Saint Bident
snippet:
Saint Bident -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : This spear caters towards Faith-oriented builds, working either being infused with a Lightning Gem or buffed with resins or spells, such as Lightning Blade. Oddly enough, the Heavy infusion seems to be the only non-elemental infusion to benefit this spear. It is also one of the longest in its class, save for the Gargoyle Flame Spear and similar in length to the Lothric Knight Long Spear, which is a pike.

title: Demon's Spear
snippet:
Demon's Spear -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Deals Lightning Damage as well as Thrust damage and though it can get [https://darksouls.fandom.com/wiki/Damage_(Dark_Souls)#Counter_Damage Counter Damage], the AR being split between Physical and Lightning reduces the bonus' effectiveness. The Demon's Spear is the longest spear in the game, with the second longest being Silver Knight Spear and cooperatively features a moveset extremely well suited to exploiting the spear's length. Use the strong attack with care as it has a long build-up and cannot be cancelled.

title: Dragon Knight
snippet:
Dragon Knight -  Dark Souls II - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : These foes can dual wield, though their attack speed isn't that impressive. They can perform guard breaks on the player and will take an Estus when injured. The player can exploit their distance by using ranged attacks such as Poison Arrows. Sweeping weapons with high poise damage, such as the Greatsword, are also effective, allowing the player to stun-lock them with several strikes before moving back, completely avoiding damage. Due to their large health pool, it's best to lure them out one at a time to avoid being overwhelmed.

They are very weak to lightning based miracles such as Lightning Spear.

title: Lord Gwyn's Firstborn
snippet:
Lord Gwyn's Firstborn -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Lord Gwyn's firstborn, the God of War, inherited the sunlight from his father, Gwyn, the Lord of Sunlight. He once wore an ancient ring capable of boosting the strength of miracles. He was said to have had respect only for arms and nothing else, and wielded the Sunlight Blade and Great Lightning Spear miracles.

His foolishness led to the stripping of his deific status and the expunging of his existence from history, with his name being forgotten. Sunlight Blade, which had the power to boost a weapon with rays of the sun in the form of lightning, was left on Gwyn's coffin, perhaps as a final farewell.

title: Lightning Spear
snippet:
Lightning Spear -  Dark Souls - spell - notes 
 notes : Using a bow or binoculars' zoom-in feature to manually aim slightly to the left of a stationary target and then using lightning spear can ensure accuracy against targets not within lock-on range. Bows are more useful for the task as their zoom-in has a crosshair.
